comments.author: @user-w2i1n
comments.text: A 22% value-added tax; an excess of public-sector employees—a byproduct of rewarding political loyalty; an oligopolistic structure that sustains obscene profit margins for sectors such as soft-drink bottlers, personal-care products, and pharmaceuticals; exorbitant insurance premiums; and the squandering of public funds on superfluous expenditures—frequently exposed in the press—all compounded by a crushing tax burden. This heavy load serves to fund the salaries of public-sector workers who would likely never command such compensation in the private sector—especially given that their résumés, rather than showcasing genuine merit, reveal a recurring pattern of political maneuvering to secure a government post every five years, following each election cycle. It would be a welcome change if they were to step down, start engaging in truly productive work, and, in doing so, truly honor the democracy of that small, cherished nation...
